clue.text: Whip on prof's rear and quickly show your bits

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the whip comes after the professor's tail
a professor's rear is the back end of the word prof, its last letter

parts.note: to whip is to lash

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone whipping a professor's backside and then exposing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' points at the end of 'prof', not of 'prof's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash is to expose yourself briefly, a quick showing of intimate parts.

clue.text: City welcoming hot Dutch woman

indicators.note: a city welcoming visitors takes them inside it, so the other letters go into the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
something hot is fashionable, or in

explanation.surface: A city warmly receiving an attractive woman from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch woman' reads as one phrase, but 'Dutch' belongs to the wordplay and 'woman' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a female given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Southern fellow framing present is photographer

indicators.note: the outer letters frame, or surround, the word for present like a picture

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: A man from the south framing a gift turns out to be a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means the time now.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Snowdon, Antony Armstrong-Jones, was a celebrated British society photographer married to Princess Margaret.

clue.text: Police to arrest a trainee English stockholder?

indicators.note: police arresting someone take hold of them, so the letter goes inside the police word

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
a cub is a trainee, as in a cub reporter

explanation.surface: Police detaining a young English trainee who holds company stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' suggests shares, but it is a cube that holds the makings of stock for cooking; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat cube is a compressed block of flavouring that, dissolved, makes stock for soups and gravy.

clue.text: Foreign fighter heading to Malta with retired soldier

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of Malta
retired means drawn back, so the soldier word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A foreign warplane flying to Malta carrying a soldier who has left the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The MiG is a Russian jet, a fighter aircraft from abroad.

clue.text: Serpent is more evil, doing Bluth's head in!

indicators.note: doing someone in is killing them off, so a letter is removed from the evil word
completes the phrase doing in, meaning getting rid of the letter

parts.note: badder is a jokey comparative of bad, more evil

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter, here of Bluth's

explanation.surface: A snake, nastier than ever, driving the Bluth family to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bluths are the family in the US sitcom Arrested Development; 'doing ... in' removes B from BADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a kind of serpent.

clue.text: Salt limit Brown has admitted 'primarily idiotic'

parts.note: a cap is a limit, as on spending

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the letter goes inside the brown word

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the first letter of idiotic

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown imposing a salt limit, described as idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is the old word for a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced seaman, and a captain is a sailor of rank.

clue.text: Naughty baron at it in transport bound for docks?

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is disorderly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misbehaving nobleman getting up to mischief on a train heading for the port.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat train is a railway service timed to connect with a ship's sailing at a port.

clue.text: Tight garment that you must wear for fight

indicators.note: wearing something puts you inside it, so the letter goes into the reworked garment
tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A snug item of clothing you are obliged to put on for a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' (drunk) shuffles GARMENT into ARGMENT, which then 'must wear' U.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a quarrel, a verbal fight.

clue.text: Given good spirit, but aim to drink beer

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the beer goes inside the aim word

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Courage is a British brand of beer

explanation.surface: Someone cheered up, though their goal was to have a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Courage is a long-established English brewery and beer brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being encouraged is being heartened, given confidence or spirit.

clue.text: Sleep around, having accepted liberal proposal

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so the letter goes inside
around signals turning the sleep word back to front

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A promiscuous suggestion that a liberal has gone along with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep around' reads as one phrase, but 'around' is the reversal signal on NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme put forward, a proposal.

clue.text: Plain awful to be full of flu essentially

indicators.note: being full of something holds it inside, so the letter goes into the awful word

parts.note: awful means bad

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle, here of flu

explanation.surface: It is simply dreadful to be bunged up with flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adverb meaning simply, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald statement is plain and blunt, without embellishment.

clue.text: Y-fronts less than penny? Worker gets small

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: Men's briefs costing under a penny, and a worker buys small ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are a British brand-name style of men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Dash of liquorice infusing bold sweet

indicators.note: something infusing another soaks into it, so the letter goes inside the bold word

parts.note: daring means bold

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, so just the first letter of liquorice

explanation.surface: A little liquorice flavouring a striking confection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like a confection but is the term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and darling are both endearments for a loved one.

clue.text: Cost to bring in northern musician at one time

indicators.note: bringing something in places it inside, so the letter goes into the cost word

parts.note: a price is a cost

explanation.surface: What it cost to book a northern performer years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince was the American singer and guitarist who died in 2016, hence a musician of the past.

clue.text: We hire inn out to have a drink

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We rent a pub to go out for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhine wine is a hock, a white wine from the Rhine valley, so a drink.

clue.text: European and Scotsman chasing after Italian

indicators.note: the Scot chases, so comes after, the Italian

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
Ian is the crossword's stock Scottish name

explanation.surface: A European and a Scot pursuing an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romanian is a native of Romania, a European country.

clue.text: Male bohemian socialist killed for beliefs?

parts.note: arty describes a bohemian, artistic type
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: An arty left-wing man executed for his political convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To be martyred is to be put to death for refusing to renounce your faith.

clue.text: Large bitter drunk by head of Indigo Books

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters of bitter are shuffled
the head is the first letter, here of Indigo

explanation.surface: A big pint of bitter downed by the boss of a bookshop chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Indigo is a Canadian bookshop chain; bitter is a British style of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Libretti are the texts of operas, often called books.

clue.text: Spooner said "fire inexperienced tool!"

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the first sounds are exchanged

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: Spooner ordering the dismissal of a hopeless new hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack saw is a type of saw, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Temporary head of state is concerning chap

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A news item: a man about whom a caretaker leader has concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of an absent or underage monarch, standing in for a time.

clue.text: Rubbish cover on Bentley in car storage

indicators.note: the letter goes in the car storage word

parts.note: a garage stores a car

indicators.note: the cover on a word is its top, so the first letter of Bentley in a down clue

explanation.surface: A useless dust sheet over a Bentley parked in the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish cover' reads as one phrase; 'Rubbish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is the American word for rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Recreational vehicle seen on the Strand?

definitions.text: Recreational vehicle seen on the Strand?

parts.words: Recreational vehicle seen on the Strand?
parts.note: the Strand is a London street, but a strand is also a shore, where a fun car is driven on the sand

explanation.surface: A camper van spotted on London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street; with a small s, a strand is a seashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach buggy is a small open off-road car built for driving on sand.

clue.text: Want to get under British player trying to mate?

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting under places the want word below the abbreviation

parts.note: to want is to lack

explanation.surface: A British performer eager to find a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' suggests romance, but it is checkmate in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Black is one of the two sides in chess, a player seeking checkmate.

clue.text: Con parting from last of loot is a wrench

indicators.note: the letter parts company from the con word, so it is removed

parts.note: a trick is a con

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word loot, the one that parts company

explanation.surface: A swindler leaving his share of the stolen goods is a painful wrench.
explanation.definitionFit: To rick is to sprain or twist, as in wrench a muscle.

clue.text: Poll: Her Maj getting more sexy?

parts.note: to poll is to cut the hair, a cut
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A survey asking whether the Queen is becoming more attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like a survey but is the old verb for cropping hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuter means more attractive, with the question mark admitting the stretch to sexier.

clue.text: Good opportunities get drinks

parts.note: ins are openings or opportunities, as in an in with someone

explanation.surface: Good chances to have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gins are measures of the spirit gin, so drinks.

clue.text: Criminal pals crept around a pair one shouldn't upset?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter
criminal means bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crooked friends sneaked about a couple who must not be disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'upset the applecart', to spoil a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Applecarts are the things proverbially not to be upset, from the idiom about ruining plans.

clue.text: Indy setter shortened piece of wordplay

indicators.note: shortened means the setter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Punk is a setter of Independent crosswords

explanation.surface: An Independent compiler trimmed a bit of clever wording.
explanation.walkthrough: Indy is a nickname for the Independent newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun is a play on words, a piece of wordplay.

clue.text: Once more bring round a new rake for landscaping

indicators.note: landscaping reshapes ground, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Buy a fresh garden rake to bring the lawn back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawaken is to rouse again, bringing someone back to consciousness.

clue.text: One pumping round into Republican? Au contraire!

indicators.note: into first suggests putting the round inside
the opposite holds, so the Republican goes inside the round instead

parts.note: a heat is a round of a competition

explanation.surface: Someone pumping lead into a Republican, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au contraire!' flips 'round into Republican' so R goes into HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the organ that pumps blood around the body.
